questionReadAloudEn:
Name and describe the type of
government in Ancient Greece.
answerReadAloudEn:
Ancient Greece had a direct
democracy in which people voted
on each law and decision the
society made.
questionReadAloudEs:
Nombra y describe el tipo de
gobierno que existía en la Antigua
Grecia.
answerReadAloudEs:
Antiguamente Grecia tenía una
democracia directa en la que la
gente votó sobre cada ley decisión
tomada por la sociedad.

questionReadAloudEn:
Name and describe the type of
government in Ancient Rome.
answerReadAloudEn:
Ancient Rome had a republic
(representative democracy) in
which people voted for leaders
who made the laws and decisions
for a society.
questionReadAloudEs:
Nombra y describe el tipo de
gobierno que existía en la Antigua
Roma.
answerReadAloudEs:
La antigua Roma tenía una
república (democracia
representativa) en la que el
pueblo votaba por sus líderes
quién hizo las leyes y decisiones
para una sociedad.

questionReadAloudEn:
Ancient Romans created the concept of
separation of powers.
What does separation of powers
mean?
answerReadAloudEn:
It means the government is
split into three branches
each with its own
responsibilities.
questionReadAloudEs:
Los antiguos romanos crearon el concepto de
separación de poderes.
¿Qué significa la separación de
poderes?
answerReadAloudEs:
Significa El gobierno está
dividido en tres ramas, cada
una con sus propias
responsabilidades.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​Who controlled the American
 colonies?
 2.​Why were the colonists angry?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The British monarchy
 2.​Colonists had no power to make
 laws or control taxes

questionReadAloudEn:
What is the main purpose in the
Declaration of Independence?
answerReadAloudEn:
Tells the British Monarchy that the
Colonists want their own government

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​Who fought the
 Revolutionary War?
 2.​What happened after the war?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Britain and the colonists
 2.​The United States became its own
 nation with a Representative
 Democracy

questionReadAloudEn:
Name that Founding Father!
 1)​Who was the first president of the
 United States?
 2)​Who wrote the Declaration of
 Independence?
 3)​Who wrote the Constitution?
answerReadAloudEn:
1)​George Washington
 2)​Thomas Jefferson
 3)​James Madison

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What were the Articles of
 Confederation?
 2.​Why did they fail?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The first rulebook for the U.S.
 Government
 2.​They gave too much freedom to
 state government and not enough
 power to the federal government

questionReadAloudEn:
America’s first two political parties
were the Federalists and Anti-Federalists.
Briefly describe each of their beliefs
about government.
answerReadAloudEn:
●​ Federalists: supported a strong
 federal government and the
 Constitution
 ●​ Anti-Federalists: supported more
 power for the states and pushed
 to have a Bills of Rights to protect
 individual freedoms

questionReadAloudEn:
The Constitution is the supreme law of the land.
What does that mean?
answerReadAloudEn:
The rulebook for the United
States that says how the
government works and what
power it has

questionReadAloudEn:
The Constitution is the supreme law of the land.
What does that mean?
answerReadAloudEn:
A set of written rules that states
how the government works and
what power it has

questionReadAloudEn:
What do articles 1-3 of the Constitution
create?
answerReadAloudEn: The three branches of government.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is an Amendment?
 2.​How many Amendments are
 there?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​An Amendment is a change to the
 Constitution
 2.​27 Amendments

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is the Bill of Rights?
 2.​What does the Bill of Rights
 protect?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The first 10 Amendments to the
 Constitution
 2.​The Bill of Rights protects rights
 and freedoms for people in the US

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the five freedoms guaranteed
in the First Amendment?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Religion
 2.​Assembly
 3.​Press
 4.​Petition
 5.​Speech

questionReadAloudEn:
What right is guaranteed in the
 Second Amendment?
answerReadAloudEn: The right to bear arms (own a gun)

questionReadAloudEn:
The Fourth Amendment protects
against unreasonable search and
seizure.
 Explain this right.
answerReadAloudEn:
Except in some emergencies, the police
cannot search or take your property
without:
1. a reason supported by evidence
(probable cause)
2. legal permission from a judge (a
warrant)

questionReadAloudEn:
1The Fifth Amendment guarantees rights
in a criminal trial, including due process
and protection against self
incrimination.
 2
 Explain these two rights.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Due process:
 The government must follow fair
 rules before it can punish you
2.​Protection against self incrimination: You
 don’t have to say anything or provide
 evidence that would make you look
 guilty.

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the three branches
of government and what are their
jobs?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Legislative: writes laws
 2.​Executive: carries out laws
 3.​Judicial: interprets laws

questionReadAloudEn:
What is the purpose of checks and
balances?
answerReadAloudEn:
Checks and balances makes sure that
one branch of government doesn’t have
all the power.
Example: The president can veto laws passed by Congress.

questionReadAloudEn:

 legislative branch of the Federal
 Government?
 2.​What are the two parts?
answerReadAloudEn:

4c)
 1.​Congress
 2.​The Senate and the House of
 Representatives

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​Who is the leader of the
 executive branch of the Federal
 Government?
 2.​Who advises this leader?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The President
 2.​The “Cabinet” of advisors who are
 called Secretaries
Examples: Secretary of Education, Secretary of Defense

questionReadAloudEn:
The judicial branch is made up
of many different courts.
What is the highest court in the
judicial branch?
answerReadAloudEn: The Supreme Court

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the two key differences
between Democrats and Republicans?
answerReadAloudEn:
Democrats believe the government
should do more to help people through
laws and programs.
Republicans believe the government
should have less control and people
should rely more on themselves.

questionReadAloudEn:
What kind of government does the
United States have? Explain it.
answerReadAloudEn:
Representative Democracy:
Citizens vote for representatives
who then make the laws. Citizens
don’t vote directly on federal laws.

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the two ways to become
a US citizen?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Natural Born:
 Be born in the USA, or have
 parents who are citizens at
 the time of their birth
 2.​Naturalized:
 Move to the USA, apply, and
 pass a test

questionReadAloudEn: What are rights?
answerReadAloudEn:
Freedoms and powers people can
choose to use.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What are civic
 responsibilities?
 2.​What is one major example of
 a civic responsibility?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Duties people are required to
 do for their city, state, or
 country.
 2.​ Following laws

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the two major rights and
responsibilities of citizens that
residents don’t have?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​jury duty
 2.​voting

questionReadAloudEn:
One civic responsibility everyone (citizens and
residents) has in the United States is to pay taxes.
 1.​What are taxes?
 2.​What are taxes used for?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Taxes are money people pay
 to the government
 2.​Taxes are used to pay for
 public goods and services
Examples: public schools, roads, parks, etc.

questionReadAloudEn: What does the 10th Amendment say?
answerReadAloudEn:
Powers not given to the federal
government go to the states and
the people

questionReadAloudEn:
What is federalism?
The idea that the federal government and state
governments share and divide power in a nation.
answerReadAloudEn:
The idea that the federal
government and state governments
share and divide power in a nation.

questionReadAloudEn:
The Massachusetts Constitution protects all civil
rights in the United States Constitution, and adds
more. For example, freedom of speech is
protected in the US Constitution and the MA
Constitution. However, the MA Constitution
includes additional rights that are not found in
the US Constitution.
What major right is protected in
the MA Constitution but not in the
US Constitution?
answerReadAloudEn:
The right to a free, public
 education

questionReadAloudEn:
The Necessary and Proper
Clause in the Constitution is also called
the Elastic Clause. What does the
Elastic Clause do?
answerReadAloudEn:
The Elastic Clause allows Congress to stretch
its powers - do things beyond what’s written
in the Constitution.

questionReadAloudEn: What is judicial review?
answerReadAloudEn:
Judicial review is when the Supreme Court
decides whether laws or government actions
follow the Constitution.

questionReadAloudEn:
Label the map with the two
sides of the Civil War. Circle who won.

The time before the Civil War there was
growing tension between the North and the
South in the USA. What was the main cause
of this tension?
answerReadAloudEn:
The North and the South disagreed about
slavery. The South wanted to keep slavery, but
the North wanted to limit or end it.

questionReadAloudEn:
What did the 13th amendment
do?
answerReadAloudEn: Abolished slavery

questionReadAloudEn:
What did the 14th amendment
do?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Gave anyone born in the US
 citizenship
2.​Gave equal rights to all
 citizens including due process

questionReadAloudEn:
What did the 15th amendment
do?
answerReadAloudEn:
Gave men of color the
right to vote

questionReadAloudEn:
What is freedom of the
press?
answerReadAloudEn:
AAA
Journalists have the right to report
news without the government
stopping or controlling them.

questionReadAloudEn:
Why was free press included in the
First Amendment?
answerReadAloudEn:
●​ To help inform citizens of the truth
●​ To make sure that the government
 is not doing something unfair.

questionReadAloudEn:
Political cartoons are part of the press.
What is the purpose of a political
cartoon? Below is an example.
answerReadAloudEn:
Political cartoons use pictures and
humor to show ideas and criticize
the government in an interesting
way.
